eng-02|eng-07.note: The Eiffel Tower expanding in heat, and the Chenab Bridge's height, which only uses the tower as a comparison.

eng-09|eng-falkirk-wheel.note: Both lift boats, by different means: the Panama Canal uses gravity-fed locks, the Falkirk Wheel a balanced rotating lift.

eng-09|eng-suez-canal.note: Two different canals: Suez has no locks and was blocked by one ship in 2021; Panama lifts ships through locks by gravity.

eng-great-pyramid-precision|hist-01.note: hist-01 uses the pyramid only as a date marker for Cleopatra; the other is about how accurately it was built.

geo-04|space-09.note: Tallest mountains measured different ways on Earth, and Olympus Mons on Mars.

geo-amazon-discharge|geo-lake-baikal.note: Baikal is about how much fresh water one lake stores; the Amazon card is about how much river flow reaches the sea.

gk-png-languages|soc-half-world-23-langu.note: One is about a single country holding 840 languages; the other about half of humanity speaking just 23. Both mention endangered languages only in passing.

math-02|math-seven-shuffles.note: math-02 counts the possible orders of a deck; the other says how many riffle shuffles it takes to randomise one.

math-ramsey-party|soc-02.note: Ramsey's theorem about guaranteed patterns among six people, and the small-world finding about chains of acquaintance.

pol-04|pol-constitution-lifespan.note: pol-04 is about the length of India's constitution in words; the other is about how many years constitutions typically survive.

pol-finland-women-mps|pol-panchayat-wome.note: One is about reserved local council seats in India since 1992; the other about the first women elected to a national parliament in 1907.

pol-india-first-election|pol-secret-ball.note: India's first election and its symbol-marked ballot boxes, and the origin of the secret ballot in 1850s Australia.

sci-02|sci-mitochondria-origin.note: sci-02 counts bacteria living in the body today; the other is about mitochondria descending from bacteria swallowed long ago.

sci-03|sci-triple-point.note: sci-03 is about water being densest at 4 degrees so ice floats; the other is about the triple point where it boils and freezes at once.

sci-05|sci-blue-whale-heart.note: Different animals and facts: a blue whale's heart rate when diving, and an octopus having three hearts.

soc-02|soc-friendship-paradox.note: soc-02 is about chains of acquaintance between any two people; the other is about why your friends average more friends than you.

space-01|space-sun-mass-loss.note: space-01 is about how long light takes to leave the Sun; the other is about how much mass the Sun converts to energy each second.

tech-arpanet-first-message|tech-email-at.note: The first ARPANET message of 1969 (LO), and the first email and the choice of the at sign in 1971.
